analysis:
The PR changes two test-only Swift files. In each, a switch over MLXServerGenerationEvent gains a `case .logprobs:` arm that ignores the event. Those are Qwen36ProductionCanaryTests.swift (head lines 394-395, in `collect`) and FlintAnswerStopTests.swift (head line 130, in `FlintStreamOutcome.record`). The change only keeps the test event switches exhaustive after a new `.logprobs` event case was added to the server event enum. That enum change is not in the supplied evidence.

The edits touch no production code. They do not affect keys (A-002, A-003), attestation, authorization (A-016), the coordinator-provider WebSocket contract (TB-002), or prefix-cache storage (T-041). The Qwen live canary is gated by the DARKBLOOM_LIVE_MLX_TESTS and DARKBLOOM_LIVE_MLX_QWEN36 environment variables. It sets DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0, so it exercises no at-rest cache artifacts. Its default model and image paths are local temp paths and are not security-relevant.

Remaining integration question: the production change that introduces `.logprobs` is outside this batch. That change should be reviewed for whether logprobs add new data exposure on the provider-to-coordinator response path. For example, they should be encrypted and fail closed in line with T-008, and a consumer-requested logprobs payload must not bypass the sealing path. These test-only edits are not evidence for or against that.
